answer: Treating network identity as a fragile fable invites disaster when ghosts try to hijack the throttle. A cryptographic proof-of-stake trellis binds every virtual piston to staked capital, forcing sybils to burn real currency for every phantom cylinder they cast. Just as a spectrographic prism splits light to expose adulterated fuel, this economic friction exposes fake nodes by making mass replication prohibitively expensive, though determined cartels with deep reserves can still breach the threshold if capital limits drift.
